etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English anoyaunce (rare form of noyaunce), from Old French anuiance, anoiance, from the verb anuier (“to cause problems”), equivalent to annoy +‎ -ance. Compare French ennui.

definitions.definition: (countable) An act or instance of annoying.
(uncountable) The psychological state of being annoyed or irritated.

quote.citation: 2022, Candice Carty-Williams, People Person, Trapeze, page 273:
quote.text: ‘I’m not annoyed with you,’ Lizzie said, putting a hand on Dimple’s shoulder. ‘Well, I am. But you’re my sister. So the annoyance is nothing new.’
